steps.label: Raw leads
steps.note: A sheet of firms comes in and becomes records the engine can work.

parts.label: A sheet in any layout is read
parts.what: The AI reads the header and a sample; a person can correct any column.

parts.label: Every website on the sheet is checked
parts.what: Each site is visited, and the firm's own pages are found from it.

parts.label: A firm is searched for when its website is wrong
parts.what: The finder is built and careful, but it runs only from the command line.

parts.label: Rows sorted into Batch 1 and Batch 2
parts.what: All five fields means Batch 1, a name with gaps means Batch 2, and a row with no firm name is discarded instead of becoming "Unknown Firm".

parts.label: What was discarded, shown and downloadable
parts.what: Every rejected row with its number and the reason.

steps.label: Enrichment
steps.note: Everything the engine can learn about a firm, from its own pages and the open web.

parts.label: The firm's own site read end to end
parts.what: Twelve pages today where the brief asks for five, with the phone and address from the listing instead.

parts.label: Fee model, practice, size and tier read from the site
parts.what: Read by patterns and by the AI, and never guessed when the site does not say.

parts.label: The people, with their titles and roles
parts.what: Owners, office managers and attorneys, from the pages and the AI's reading.

parts.label: Addresses found on the site and in search
An address worked out from a name and the firm's domain
parts.what: Eleven patterns, the firm's own pattern learned from addresses already found.

parts.label: Every address checked before it is used
LinkedIn profiles for the firm and its people
parts.what: From search results only. LinkedIn itself is never opened.

parts.label: The Google Business Profile read
parts.what: Name, category, address, phone, website, rating and review count, kept whole and shown on the lead; the phone and address go onto the firm's record.
parts.waiting_on: The Google Business Profile and its reviews

parts.label: Reviews read for what they say
parts.what: The listing's reviews are kept word for word and shown on the lead; the AI quotes one when it names a pain. No review site is ever scraped.
parts.waiting_on: The Google Business Profile and its reviews

parts.label: The firm's phone number
parts.what: The main line, from the site or the Google listing; nobody's direct line yet.

parts.label: The AI names what hurts, quoting the record
parts.what: Every pain must quote one line of the firm's record; anything it cannot quote is thrown away.

parts.label: An enrichment report for each lead
parts.what: The firm, the people, the reviews, the listing and the pain analysis as one document.

parts.label: Firms enriched in batches of 250, Batch 1 first, starting by itself
parts.what: Today a person selects leads and presses Research.

steps.label: Handover
steps.note: The engine drafts and keeps the record. Sending stays with you or the vendor.

parts.label: Seven checks decide whether a lead is ready
parts.what: Site read, fits the profile, a named decision-maker, an address, a checked address, a profile, emails drafted.

parts.label: The email journey, day by day
parts.what: Nine emails over four weeks, each written from the lead's own proof; the words and the days can be changed for every lead.

parts.label: Every email is signed, and says how to stop
parts.what: The engine appends who it is from and an opt-out line to every draft. The name, reply address and postal address US law requires come from config/sender.yml, and the Email journey screen says what is still blank.

parts.label: What a firm's answer means, on record
parts.what: Replied, meeting, not now, opted out, won, lost — each moves the lead and is kept in its history.

parts.label: Actual leads kept as a pool, each journey saved as it lands
parts.what: Today the panel works the checks out afresh on every visit.

parts.label: A vendor chosen, a handover document written, leads marked as given
parts.what: No vendor, no handover record and no note of who received which lead exists yet.

outside.label: The AI reader
outside.what: Reads each firm's site for its fee model, practice, people and gaps, reads an uploaded sheet's columns, and writes the pain analysis.
outside.cost: Paid per firm read. Measured here at well under a penny a firm.

outside.label: Address checking
outside.what: Checks every address before a lead can be handed over, and lets the engine work out the addresses it could not find on a site.

outside.label: The Google Business Profile and its reviews
outside.what: Finds each firm's Google listing through Google's own API -- phone, address, category, website, rating and review count -- and keeps its reviews, which the AI quotes when it names a pain. Serper's key does the same job when this one is blank. Nothing is ever scraped off a Google page.
outside.cost: Free for the first 1,000 lookups a month on Google's own API; then paid per lookup.

outside.label: Web search
outside.what: Google search at volume, for LinkedIn profiles, company pages and addresses in snippets, and a second way to the business listing and its reviews. Without it the engine falls back to DuckDuckGo, which stops us after a few hundred queries.

summary: 15 of 24 parts are built, 3 are partly there and 6 are still to come. 6 built parts are idle until a key is set.
